snapshot.stmt: Let \(E_1,E_0\) be compact metric spaces.  Under weak convergence of an ordered pair of marginal probability measures, the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in the weak topology.  Consequently, for every continuous function \(\varphi:E_1\times E_0\to\mathbb R\), the minimum and maximum of \(H\mapsto\int\varphi\,dH\) over the coupling set vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair, and the associated optimizer correspondences are upper hemicontinuous.

assumptions.ass:fixed-marginals: The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).

source.locator: Main continuity theorem and the Berge maximum-theorem consequence, pp. 471--481
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1. Let X and Y be separable metrizable spaces and let φ : P(X) × P(Y) ⇉ P(X × Y) be defined: φ(μ,ν) = {τ ∈ P(X × Y) | τ_X = μ, τ_Y = ν}. The correspondence φ is continuous. According to Berge's maximum theorem, if W and Z are topological spaces and Φ : W ⇉ Z is a continuous correspondence with nonempty compact values, and f : W × Z → ℝ is continuous then (i) the function m(w) = max_{z∈Φ(w)} f(w,z) is continuous, and (ii) the correspondence β defined by β(w) = {z ∈ Z | f(w,z) = m(w)} is upper-hemicontinuous.

thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transf.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Positive definiteness makes both arm columns nonzero, so the quotient map from \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) onto \(\mathcal B_Z\) is well defined and surjective.  The projective equivalence relation gives
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)\Longleftrightarrow C=BT,
\qquad T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0),\quad t_1t_0\ne0.
\tag{1}
\]
For such \(T\),
\[
S_{BT}=T^\top S_BT,
\qquad S_{BT}^{-1}=T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^\top)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Substitution in the trace formula and cyclicity cancel every factor of \(T\), proving \(g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c)\).  The uncontrolled term is basis independent, so the residual and worst-endpoint loss are invariant as well.  Any invariant function is constant on every fiber of a surjection; its extrema over an inverse image equal those over the quotient set, and an attained optimizer pulls back exactly to the inverse image of the quotient optimizer set.  This is an exact transfer for the positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's larger published pseudoinverse class. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) be the unquotiented positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, and let \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).  Then \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) is surjective, and
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C=B\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)
\quad\text{for some }t_1t_0\ne0.
\]
For every such diagonal \(T\), every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), and every \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\),
\[
g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
\ell_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=\ell_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
w(q_Z(BT))=w(q_Z(B)).
\]
Consequently, for every nonempty \(K\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), the infima and suprema of each displayed pullback criterion over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) equal those over \(K\), and every attained optimizer correspondence is the inverse image of its quotient correspondence.  This theorem concerns only the rank-two restriction; the published pseudoinverse strata are carried by \(\mathcal B_Z^+\).

defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:zhao-well-defined-ordinary-domain: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the unquotiented positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's published pseudoinverse basis domain, not the full published domain.  Define \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\), where \(\mathcal B_Z\) is its quotient by independent nonzero arm-column rescaling.

assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

lem:ht-affine-drift.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).  Def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  Mutual exclusivity implies
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}=\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Exposure positivity permits division, so symmetry gives \(\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)=-2n\).  Therefore
\[
h(c)=h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=h(0)+2c/n.
\]
Subtracting the endpoint gains yields the displayed formula for \(w(B)\).

To prove non-equivalence, put \(a_e=2c_e/n\) and define on a formal endpoint-gain pair \(x\)
\[
\Phi(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
\qquad \Psi(x)=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}.
\]
If \(\Phi=\Psi+K\) for all \(x\), evaluating at \((t,0)\) gives \(K=a_U\), while evaluating at \((0,t)\) for \(t\ge a_U-a_L\) gives \(K=a_L\).  This contradicts \(c_L<c_U\). \(\square\)

\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.

If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).

thm:moment-complete-finite-epsilon-solve.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\{(b_1,b_0):\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ B^{\top}\Omega B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty.  It is closed in a product of two spheres and hence compact; prop:kappa-exhaustion identifies its finite sign quotient with \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  On (1),
\[
\lVert(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The trace formulas in def:gain-loss, the resolvent identity, and (2) make both endpoint losses, and hence their maximum \(w\), continuous on \(K_\kappa\).  The refinement moduli in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) turn this compactness argument into an effective uniform-continuity modulus: for every positive rational \(\rho\), the inclusion oracles terminate with a rational chart diameter \(d(\rho)>0\) such that two feasible representatives in the same box of diameter at most \(d(\rho)\) have losses differing by at most \(\rho\).

Cover each normalized projective factor by the finitely many signed pivot charts in def:branch-bound-handle.  Fix a rational \(\rho>0\) with \(4\rho<\varepsilon\), and bisect all retained boxes until their diameters are at most \(\min\{\varepsilon,d(\rho)\}\).  This is a finite depth and produces finitely many boxes.  The exact feasibility interface decides every box, including boxes whose feasible intersection lies entirely on
\(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  In each feasible box, exact feasible-child selection and repeated nested refinement give the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible point \(B_C\).  The endpoint inclusion oracles and their effective arithmetic moduli then terminate with outward rational bounds \(\underline q_C,\overline q_C\) satisfying
\[
w(B_C)-\rho\le\underline q_C\le w(B_C)
\le\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\rho.
\tag{3}
\]
Uniform continuity supplies the valid box lower bound
\[
\lambda_C:=\underline q_C-\rho
\le\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B).
\tag{4}
\]
Set \(L_\varepsilon=\min_C\lambda_C\), \(U_\varepsilon=\min_C\overline q_C\), and choose \(B_\varepsilon\) from a box attaining the latter minimum.  A box containing a compact-class minimizer, (3), and (4) give
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\rho\le L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\rho.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \(U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon<\varepsilon\).  Prune only boxes certified infeasible or having a valid lower bound strictly above the incumbent upper bound.  No box meeting \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) can satisfy either condition, so the union \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) of unpruned quotient boxes contains \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  The prescribed refinement gives \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

Every stage terminates: the chart cover and subdivision depth are finite, and every requested feasibility, arithmetic, and inclusion-oracle refinement terminates by def:certified-input-interface.  The finite record is exactly \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\) of def:certified-output.  Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in (5) and the mesh bound proves convergence of both certified gaps.  The construction is instance dependent and supplies neither a uniform complexity bound nor an SDP reduction. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[

\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes. defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:certified-output: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\). defs.def:argmax-correspondences:
On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), define the primary full-quotient equality correspondences
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0),
\]
which may be empty. assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:kappa-feasibility: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:product-coupling-zero: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

node.statement:
For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.
node.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\{(b_1,b_0):\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ B^{\top}\Omega B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty.  It is closed in a product of two spheres and hence compact; prop:kappa-exhaustion identifies its finite sign quotient with \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  On (1),
\[
\lVert(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The trace formulas in def:gain-loss, the resolvent identity, and (2) make both endpoint losses, and hence their maximum \(w\), continuous on \(K_\kappa\).  The refinement moduli in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) turn this compactness argument into an effective uniform-continuity modulus: for every positive rational \(\rho\), the inclusion oracles terminate with a rational chart diameter \(d(\rho)>0\) such that two feasible representatives in the same box of diameter at most \(d(\rho)\) have losses differing by at most \(\rho\).

Cover each normalized projective factor by the finitely many signed pivot charts in def:branch-bound-handle.  Fix a rational \(\rho>0\) with \(4\rho<\varepsilon\), and bisect all retained boxes until their diameters are at most \(\min\{\varepsilon,d(\rho)\}\).  This is a finite depth and produces finitely many boxes.  The exact feasibility interface decides every box, including boxes whose feasible intersection lies entirely on
\(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  In each feasible box, exact feasible-child selection and repeated nested refinement give the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible point \(B_C\).  The endpoint inclusion oracles and their effective arithmetic moduli then terminate with outward rational bounds \(\underline q_C,\overline q_C\) satisfying
\[
w(B_C)-\rho\le\underline q_C\le w(B_C)
\le\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\rho.
\tag{3}
\]
Uniform continuity supplies the valid box lower bound
\[
\lambda_C:=\underline q_C-\rho
\le\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B).
\tag{4}
\]
Set \(L_\varepsilon=\min_C\lambda_C\), \(U_\varepsilon=\min_C\overline q_C\), and choose \(B_\varepsilon\) from a box attaining the latter minimum.  A box containing a compact-class minimizer, (3), and (4) give
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\rho\le L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\rho.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \(U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon<\varepsilon\).  Prune only boxes certified infeasible or having a valid lower bound strictly above the incumbent upper bound.  No box meeting \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) can satisfy either condition, so the union \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) of unpruned quotient boxes contains \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  The prescribed refinement gives \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

Every stage terminates: the chart cover and subdivision depth are finite, and every requested feasibility, arithmetic, and inclusion-oracle refinement terminates by def:certified-input-interface.  The finite record is exactly \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\) of def:certified-output.  Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in (5) and the mesh bound proves convergence of both certified gaps.  The construction is instance dependent and supplies neither a uniform complexity bound nor an SDP reduction. \(\square\)

lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), both arm columns are nonzero, and \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=2\).  On this stratum the equivalence relation of def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain is exactly the independent nonzero rescaling relation defining \(\mathcal B_Z\).  Hence \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\) is well defined and injective.  Conversely, a rank-two positive-semidefinite \(S_B\) is positive definite, so its class has a unique preimage in \(\mathcal B_Z\).  On rank two, \(S_B^+=S_B^{-1}\).  Substitution into the two gain definitions proves equality of gains; subtraction from the same \(h(c)\) and endpoint maximization prove equality of losses. \(\square\)

lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  Since each endpoint moment matrix is positive semidefinite, congruence gives
\[
A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0.
\tag{1}
\]
Put \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Then \(S_B=Z_B^{\top}Z_B\), and cyclicity of trace yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2g_B^+(c_e)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_eZ_B\right]\\
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_e\right]
=\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The singular-value decomposition of \(Z_B\) shows that
\[
P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}
\tag{3}
\]
is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\).  Thus
\[
\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(Z_B)
=\operatorname{rank}(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)
=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The rank-two identification and equality of the ordinary and pseudoinverse gains and losses are exactly \(\texttt{lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification}\).

The zero class belongs to \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), and the ranks in (4) take values in the finite set \(\{0,1,2\}\); hence \(r_\Omega\) exists.  We construct the asserted sequence by cases.

Suppose first that \(r_\Omega=2\).  Choose \([C]_+\) with \(Z_C\) of rank two and, for a representative of \([B]_+\), put
\[
Z(t)=Z_B+tZ_C.
\tag{5}
\]
The function
\[
p(t)=\det\{Z(t)^{\top}Z(t)\}
\tag{6}
\]
is a polynomial.  Its coefficient of \(t^4\) is \(\det(Z_C^{\top}Z_C)>0\), so it is not the zero polynomial.  Choose \(t_j\downarrow0\) outside its finitely many roots.  Then \(Z(t_j)\) has rank two.  Independent normalization of its two nonzero arm columns does not alter its quotient class or projector, so it defines \([B_j]_+\in\iota(\mathcal B_Z)\).

The set of rank-two orthogonal projectors in the finite-dimensional matrix space is compact.  After taking a subsequence and relabeling, let
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty.
\tag{7}
\]
For any \(v\in\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), write \(v=Z_Bx\).  Since \(Z(t_j)x\in\operatorname{range}\{Z(t_j)\}\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(v,\operatorname{range}\{Z(t_j)\}\right)
\le |t_j|\,\lVert Z_Cx\rVert_2\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
Taking the limit in (8) gives \(P_\infty v=v\).  Therefore
\(
\operatorname{range}(P_B)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_\infty)
\), and for orthogonal projectors this is equivalent to
\[
P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\tag{9}
\]

Suppose next that \(r_\Omega=1\).  If \(B\) has rank one, take the constant sequence \(B_j=B\).  If \(B\) has rank zero, choose any rank-one class \([C]_+\), take \(B_j=C\), and put \(P_\infty=P_C\); then \(P_B=0\), so (9) again holds.  Finally, if \(r_\Omega=0\), every class has projector zero and the constant sequence suffices.  These cases prove the projector approximation for every design, including designs with no rank-two class.

By (1), (2), (7), (9), and trace monotonicity,
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty}g_{B_j}^+(c_e)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_\infty A_e)
\ge n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e)
=g_B^+(c_e)
\tag{10}
\]
for \(e=L,U\).  The uncontrolled endpoint terms do not depend on the basis.  Subtracting (10) from those terms and taking the maximum of the two endpoint residuals gives
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}w^+(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\tag{11}
\]
This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\) and \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfies
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
 \qquad P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top},
\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  Define
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[C]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(C^{\top}\Omega C).
\]
For every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), there is a sequence \(([B_j]_+)_{j\ge1}\subseteq\mathcal B_Z^+\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(S_{B_j})=r_\Omega\) and a projector \(P_\infty\) such that
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty,
\qquad P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}g_{B_j}^+(c_e)\ge g_B^+(c_e)
\quad(e\in\{L,U\}),
\qquad
\limsup_{j\to\infty}w^+(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]
If \(r_\Omega=2\), the approximating sequence may be chosen in \(\iota(\mathcal B_Z)\).
node.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  Since each endpoint moment matrix is positive semidefinite, congruence gives
\[
A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0.
\tag{1}
\]
Put \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Then \(S_B=Z_B^{\top}Z_B\), and cyclicity of trace yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2g_B^+(c_e)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_eZ_B\right]\\
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_e\right]
=\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The singular-value decomposition of \(Z_B\) shows that
\[
P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}
\tag{3}
\]
is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\).  Thus
\[
\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(Z_B)
=\operatorname{rank}(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)
=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The rank-two identification and equality of the ordinary and pseudoinverse gains and losses are exactly \(\texttt{lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification}\).

The zero class belongs to \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), and the ranks in (4) take values in the finite set \(\{0,1,2\}\); hence \(r_\Omega\) exists.  We construct the asserted sequence by cases.

Suppose first that \(r_\Omega=2\).  Choose \([C]_+\) with \(Z_C\) of rank two and, for a representative of \([B]_+\), put
\[
Z(t)=Z_B+tZ_C.
\tag{5}
\]
The function
\[
p(t)=\det\{Z(t)^{\top}Z(t)\}
\tag{6}
\]
is a polynomial.  Its coefficient of \(t^4\) is \(\det(Z_C^{\top}Z_C)>0\), so it is not the zero polynomial.  Choose \(t_j\downarrow0\) outside its finitely many roots.  Then \(Z(t_j)\) has rank two.  Independent normalization of its two nonzero arm columns does not alter its quotient class or projector, so it defines \([B_j]_+\in\iota(\mathcal B_Z)\).

The set of rank-two orthogonal projectors in the finite-dimensional matrix space is compact.  After taking a subsequence and relabeling, let
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty.
\tag{7}
\]
For any \(v\in\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), write \(v=Z_Bx\).  Since \(Z(t_j)x\in\operatorname{range}\{Z(t_j)\}\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(v,\operatorname{range}\{Z(t_j)\}\right)
\le |t_j|\,\lVert Z_Cx\rVert_2\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
Taking the limit in (8) gives \(P_\infty v=v\).  Therefore
\(
\operatorname{range}(P_B)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_\infty)
\), and for orthogonal projectors this is equivalent to
\[
P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\tag{9}
\]

Suppose next that \(r_\Omega=1\).  If \(B\) has rank one, take the constant sequence \(B_j=B\).  If \(B\) has rank zero, choose any rank-one class \([C]_+\), take \(B_j=C\), and put \(P_\infty=P_C\); then \(P_B=0\), so (9) again holds.  Finally, if \(r_\Omega=0\), every class has projector zero and the constant sequence suffices.  These cases prove the projector approximation for every design, including designs with no rank-two class.

By (1), (2), (7), (9), and trace monotonicity,
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty}g_{B_j}^+(c_e)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_\infty A_e)
\ge n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e)
=g_B^+(c_e)
\tag{10}
\]
for \(e=L,U\).  The uncontrolled endpoint terms do not depend on the basis.  Subtracting (10) from those terms and taking the maximum of the two endpoint residuals gives
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}w^+(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\tag{11}
\]
This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

thm:zhao-pseudoinverse-rank-stratified-e.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(K_0\) be the ordered field generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the finitely many entries of \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(Q(c_L)\), and \(Q(c_U)\), together with the other exactly encoded input constants.  The rational or real-algebraic input condition in def:certified-input-interface makes every element of \(K_0\) real algebraic.  By ass:exposure-positivity, every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) is strictly positive.  Hence \(\Pi^{-1}\) exists and its entries belong to \(K_0\).  The endpoint matrices \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), as well as the design covariance \(\Omega\), are positive semidefinite by their declared spaces.  These facts provide every support, division, and positivity condition used below.

\emph{Normalized semialgebraic representation of the quotient.}
By def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain, every class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable carrier, has a representative for which each arm column is either zero or has squared Euclidean norm \(n\).  It therefore suffices to work on
\[
\mathcal K=
\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\bigl(b_1=0\ \vee\ b_1^{\top}b_1=n\bigr),\quad
\bigl(b_0=0\ \vee\ b_0^{\top}b_0=n\bigr)
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is a union of four compact semialgebraic sets over \(K_0\).  For literal quotient coordinates, for each nonzero arm choose its first nonzero coordinate and require that coordinate to be positive.  The finitely many resulting semialgebraic sign charts form a one-to-one cross-section of the independent-rescaling quotient.

The objective is constant on quotient fibers, including at singular ranks.  Let \(C=\Omega^{1/2}B\), and, for \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let
\[
R_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}.
\]
The square roots are proof intermediates only; the algorithm below uses polynomial formulas in the encoded entries.  Since \(S_B=C^{\top}C\), cyclicity of trace and def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss give
\[
g_B^+(c_e)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}R_e
\right].
\tag{2}
\]
If \(C=U\Sigma V^{\top}\) is a singular-value decomposition, then
\[
C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}
=U\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(\mathbf 1\{\sigma_j>0\}\bigr)U^{\top},
\]
which is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}(C)\).  Independent nonzero rescaling of either nonzero arm column preserves that column space.  Hence (2), and therefore \(w^+(B)\), is quotient invariant at ranks zero, one, and two.  Moreover,
\[
0\preceq C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}\preceq I,
\qquad R_e\succeq0.
\]
Taking traces after multiplication by \(R_e\), and using \(n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(R_e)=h(c_e)\), yields
\[
0\le g_B^+(c_e)\le h(c_e),
\qquad
0\le \ell_B^+(c_e)\le h(c_e).
\tag{3}
\]
Equation (3) implies \(0\le w^+(B)\le H:=\max\{h(c_L),h(c_U)\}<\infty\) for every normalized representative.  Hence the attainable loss set is nonempty because the all-zero representative lies in \(\mathcal K\), and it is bounded below by \(0\) (indeed contained in \([0,H]\)); no finiteness-in-cardinality assertion is used.

\emph{Exact rank-stratified graph.}
Write \(S=S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).  Since \(\Omega\succeq0\), the matrix \(S\) is a \(2\times2\) positive-semidefinite matrix.  Its possible ranks and spectral pseudoinverses are exactly
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\operatorname{rank}(S)&\text{semialgebraic condition}&S^+\\ \hline
0&\operatorname{tr}(S)=0&0,\\[2mm]
1&\operatorname{tr}(S)>0,\ \det(S)=0&
\displaystyle\frac{S}{\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2},\\[3mm]
2&\det(S)>0&
\displaystyle\frac{\operatorname{adj}(S)}{\det(S)}.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, positive semidefiniteness makes trace zero equivalent to rank zero.  At rank one, if the nonzero eigenvalue is \(\lambda=\operatorname{tr}(S)\) and \(S=\lambda uu^{\top}\) with \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\), then \(S/\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2=\lambda^{-1}uu^{\top}=S^+\).  At rank two, positive semidefiniteness and \(\det(S)>0\) imply positive definiteness, so the last expression is the ordinary inverse.  Every denominator in (4) is strictly positive on its stated stratum; at a boundary the appropriate lower-rank row applies.

For each row of (4), substitute the displayed rational expression into the two endpoint gains.  Introduce variables \(z_L,z_U,y\) and impose
\[
z_e=h(c_e)-g_B^+(c_e)\quad(e\in\{L,U\}),
\qquad y\ge z_L,
\qquad y\ge z_U,
\qquad (y=z_L\ \vee\ y=z_U).
\tag{5}
\]
On rank one multiply the gain equalities by the strictly positive quantity \(\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2\); on rank two multiply them by the strictly positive quantity \(\det(S)\); no denominator occurs on rank zero.  Consequently (1), the applicable row of (4), and (5) form a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and strict or weak inequalities over \(K_0\).  Their union is the semialgebraic graph
\[
\mathcal G=
\{(b_1,b_0,y):(b_1,b_0)\in\mathcal K,\ y=w^+(B)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
It covers every normalized representative and all three ranks, including equality boundaries, without evaluating an inverse at a zero denominator.

\emph{Exact value isolation.}
Define
\[
\mathcal T=
\left\{t\in\mathbb R:
\exists(b_1,b_0,y)\in\mathcal G\ \text{such that}\ y\le t
\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
By (3), \(\mathcal T\) is nonempty and bounded below, and by the definitions of \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and \(\mathcal G\),
\[
\inf\mathcal T
=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+.
\tag{8}
\]
The formula in (7) is first order over a real closed field.  Apply lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination to eliminate \(b_1,b_0,z_L,z_U,y\).  The resulting quantifier-free description of \(\mathcal T\) uses finitely many polynomial sign conditions over \(K_0\).  A one-dimensional polynomial sign pattern is constant on every interval avoiding the finitely many real roots of its nonzero polynomials.  Every finite boundary point of \(\mathcal T\) is therefore a root of one of those polynomials.  By (3) and (8), \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is such a finite boundary point.  Hence \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is algebraic over \(K_0\), and thus is a real-algebraic number.

The corresponding cylindrical algebraic decomposition terminates: it begins with finitely many variables and polynomials; every projection stage forms finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and resultants; exact real-algebraic root isolation produces finitely many sign cells; and lifting repeats a finite operation through finitely many coordinates.  The equivalence in lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination certifies the sign decomposition.  Refine an isolating interval for \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) until its exactly checked width is at most the exactly encoded positive number \(\varepsilon\).  This returns rational or real-algebraic numbers \(L_\varepsilon^+\) and \(U_\varepsilon^+\) such that
\[
L_\varepsilon^+\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le U_\varepsilon^+,
\qquad
U_\varepsilon^+-L_\varepsilon^+\le\varepsilon.
\tag{9}
\]
Strict positivity and exact encoding of \(\varepsilon\) make the refinement test terminate.

\emph{Algebraic incumbent and finite certificate.}
Attainment is unnecessary.  By the defining property of an infimum and \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\exists [B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+
\quad
w^+(B)<v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\tag{10}
\]
Adjoin the real-algebraic constant \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) to the coefficient field and apply CAD lifting to (10), represented by (1), (4), and (5).  Because the formula is nonempty, CAD returns a sample point with real-algebraic coordinates.  Its normalized representative defines a basis class \([B_\varepsilon]_+\) in the note's quotient \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) of Zhao's published carrier, and
\[
w^+(B_\varepsilon)<v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
w^+(B_\varepsilon)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\tag{11}
\]
Likewise, in the finite quotient charts following (1), the weak sublevel set
\[
\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon\}
\]
is semialgebraic by the same rank-stratified formulas and is nonempty by (10).

Finally, retain the normalized quotient-chart list, the rank condition and pseudoinverse identity from (4) on every CAD cell, the projection polynomials and sign table, the algebraic sample establishing (11), and the root-isolation data establishing (9).  Exact algebraic arithmetic checks each item.  This is a finite sign, sample, and value-isolation certificate covering ranks zero, one, and two.  It supplies an \(\varepsilon\)-incumbent whether or not the infimum is attained and asserts neither outer-set convergence to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), a uniform complexity bound, nor a semidefinite-program reduction.  \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
For every rational or real-algebraic moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), a rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure terminates and returns rational or real-algebraic bounds and a basis class \([B_\varepsilon]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) in the note's quotient of Zhao's published carrier satisfying
\[
L_\varepsilon^+\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le U_\varepsilon^+,
\qquad U_\varepsilon^+-L_\varepsilon^+\le\varepsilon,
\qquad w^+(B_\varepsilon)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\]
The procedure splits \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\), represents the pseudoinverse objective by rational semialgebraic formulas on each stratum, and returns a finite checkable CAD sign, sample, and value-isolation certificate covering all strata.  The set \(\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty and semialgebraic.  No exact minimizer, outer convergence to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), uniform complexity bound, or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

\tag{5}
\]
On rank one multiply the gain equalities by the strictly positive quantity \(\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2\); on rank two multiply them by the strictly positive quantity \(\det(S)\); no denominator occurs on rank zero. \[
\mathcal G=
\{(b_1,b_0,y):(b_1,b_0)\in\mathcal K,\ y=w^+(B)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
It covers every normalized representative and all three ranks, including equality boundaries, without evaluating an inverse at a zero denominator.

\[
\mathcal T=
\left\{t\in\mathbb R:
\exists(b_1,b_0,y)\in\mathcal G\ \text{such that}\ y\le t

\tag{7}

lem:algebraic-box-feasibility-cad.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a rational signed pivot-chart box and write the \(2n\) coordinates of \((b_1,b_0)\) as \(x\).  By \(\operatorname{def{:}kappa\mbox{-}basis\mbox{-}class}\), the normalization conditions are the polynomial equations
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n b_{1i}^2=n,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^n b_{0i}^2=n.
\tag{1}
\]
Every box restriction and signed pivot restriction is a polynomial weak inequality with rational coefficients.  Since \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), each entry of \(S_B\) is a quadratic polynomial in \(x\), with coefficients in the real-algebraic coefficient field supplied by \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

Write
\[
S_B-n\kappa I_2=
\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
If the matrix in (2) is positive semidefinite, its principal minors give
\[
u\ge0,
\qquad z\ge0,
\qquad uz-v^2\ge0.
\tag{3}
\]
Conversely, suppose (3) holds.  If \(u>0\), then for every \((s,t)\in\mathbb R^2\),
\[
us^2+2vst+zt^2
=u\left(s+\frac vu t\right)^2
+\left(z-\frac{v^2}{u}\right)t^2\ge0.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(u=0\), the determinant inequality in (3) forces \(v=0\), and the quadratic form is \(zt^2\ge0\).  Thus (3) is necessary and sufficient for the matrix inequality in (2).  In particular, the use of weak inequalities retains the equality boundary.

Intersection of the chart box with the normalized feasible set is therefore represented by one existential first-order formula
\[
\exists x\;\Phi(x),
\tag{5}
\]
where \(\Phi\) is a finite conjunction of the polynomial equalities (1), the chart and box inequalities, and the three weak polynomial inequalities (3).  By \(\operatorname{lem{:}real\mbox{-}closed\mbox{-}field\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\), cylindrical algebraic decomposition returns a quantifier-free formula equivalent to (5), and exact real-algebraic sign isolation decides that formula.

It remains to verify the asserted form of the output.  During cylindrical lifting, each projection polynomial specializes to a univariate polynomial with real-algebraic coefficients.  Exact root isolation partitions the line into finitely many open sectors and root sections.  Choosing a rational point in a sector, or the isolated real-algebraic root in a section, and proceeding recursively through the finitely many coordinates produces a real-algebraic sample in every sign-invariant cell.  If one such cell satisfies \(\Phi\), its sample is an exactly feasible point.  If none does, the finite sign-invariant cell list together with the elimination trace certifies infeasibility.  Root sections are retained because every constraint is tested with its stated weak inequality, so the conclusion also holds when feasibility occurs only on a sphere boundary or on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)=\kappa\). \(\square\)

defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:

\[

defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

prop:kappa-value-exhaustion.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Exposure positivity makes every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) strictly positive, so the inverse-probability matrices occurring in \(w\) are finite.  For every nonempty \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), the compactness proposition makes \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) compact.  On its normalized representatives,
\[
 S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2.
\]
Consequently, \(B\mapsto S_B^{-1}\) is continuous there.  The trace formulas defining \(g_B(c_e)\) and \(\ell_B(c_e)\), for \(e\in\{L,U\}\), are therefore continuous in \(B\), and so is their finite maximum \(w(B)\).  These functions are invariant under the residual independent sign changes, hence descend continuously to the quotient.  Thus every displayed minimum over a nonempty \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is attained.

If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), the eigenvalue constraints give
\[
 \mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}.
\]
Minimizing the same function over these nested nonempty sets yields
\[
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
 \le
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]

The exhaustion proposition gives the set identity
\[
 \mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa,
\]
where empty threshold classes do not affect the union.  Therefore the elementary identity for an infimum over a union gives
\[
 \inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
 =
 \inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
 \inf_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
 =
 \inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\tag{1}
\]
The quotient-transfer theorem states that \(q_Z\) is surjective and that \(w\circ q_Z\) is constant on every fiber.  Hence
\[
 \inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))
 =\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\tag{2}
\]
which proves all three value equalities.

Finally, suppose \(B_Z^\star\) attains the middle infimum.  By exhaustion there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\), nesting gives \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), while \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  If \(V_Z=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)\), these two inclusions imply
\[
 V_Z
 \le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
 \le w(B_Z^\star)
 =V_Z.
\]
Thus equality holds for every such \(\kappa\).  All arguments take place on the positive-definite rank-two ordinary-inverse restriction and its exact rescaling quotient; no singular pseudoinverse class is included. \(\square\)

The trace formulas defining \(g_B(c_e)\) and \(\ell_B(c_e)\), for \(e\in\{L,U\}\), are therefore continuous in \(B\), and so is their finite maximum \(w(B)\).  These functions are invariant under the residual independent sign changes, hence descend continuously to the quotient.  Thus every displayed minimum over a nonempty \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is attained.

If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), the eigenvalue constraints give
\[
 \mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}.
\]
Minimizing the same function over these nested nonempty sets yields
\[
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
 \le
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]

The exhaustion proposition gives the set identity
\[
 \mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa,
\]
where empty threshold classes do not affect the union.  Therefore the elementary identity for an infimum over a union gives
\[
 \inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
 =
 \inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
 \inf_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
 =
 \inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\tag{1}
\]
The quotient-transfer theorem states that \(q_Z\) is surjective and that \(w\circ q_Z\) is constant on every fiber.  Hence
\[
 \inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))
 =\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\tag{2}
\]
which proves all three value equalities.

Finally, suppose \(B_Z^\star\) attains the middle infimum.  By exhaustion there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\), nesting gives \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), while \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  If \(V_Z=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)\), these two inclusions imply
\[
 V_Z
 \le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
 \le w(B_Z^\star)
 =V_Z.
\]
Thus equality holds for every such \(\kappa\).  All arguments take place on the positive-definite rank-two ordinary-inverse restriction and its exact rescaling quotient; no singular pseudoinverse class is included. \(\square\)

thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certific.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For a fixed vertex \(i\), the event \(D_{i,1}=1\) is the assignment in which \(i\) alone is treated, whereas \(D_{i,0}=1\) means that \(i\) is untreated and at least one of the other two vertices is treated.  Enumeration of the eight assignments therefore gives
\[
\pi_{i,1}=\frac4{27},
\qquad
\pi_{i,0}=\frac{10}{27},
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&i=j&i\ne j\\ \hline
\operatorname{Cov}(D_{i,1},D_{j,1})&92/729&-16/729\\
\operatorname{Cov}(D_{i,1},D_{j,0})&-40/729&68/729\\
\operatorname{Cov}(D_{i,0},D_{j,0})&170/729&8/729.
\end{array}
\tag{1}
\]
This proves the displayed \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), as well as exposure positivity and mutual exclusivity.  The Bernoulli \((1/2)\) quantile is zero on \((0,1/2]\) and one on \((1/2,1]\), so the countermonotone and comonotone products give \(c_L=-1/4\) and \(c_U=1/4\).  Substitution of \(\mu_a=1/2\) and \(\sigma_a^2=1/4\) in def:moment-matrix gives the two displayed endpoint matrices.

For a normalized representative \(B(x,y)\), put
\[
s=\mathbf1^{\top}x,
\qquad t=\mathbf1^{\top}y,
\qquad q=x^{\top}y.
\]
Direct block multiplication using (1) yields
\[
S_B=
\begin{bmatrix}
4/9-16s^2/729&-4q/27+68st/729\\
-4q/27+68st/729&2/3+8t^2/729
\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
With
\[
d=729+12t^2-36s^2-54q^2+68qst-22s^2t^2,
\tag{3}
\]
one has \(\det S_B=8d/19683\), so \(d>0\) on \(\mathcal B_{1/8}\).  Exact substitution in def:gain-loss gives
\[
\frac{31}{80}-g_B(0)=\frac{N_0}{1200d},
\tag{4}
\]
where
\[
N_0=5022q^2-4352qst+670s^2t^2+1629s^2+2148t^2.
\tag{5}
\]
The following completion makes its sign and equality set explicit:
\[
N_0
=5022\left(q-\frac{1088}{2511}st\right)^2
+1629s^2+2148t^2-\frac{685118}{2511}s^2t^2.
\tag{6}
\]
The last three terms are bilinear in \((s^2,t^2)\in[0,9]^2\).  Their values at the four vertices are
\[
0,\qquad14661,\qquad19332,\qquad\frac{368665}{31},
\]
respectively.  Bilinear interpolation therefore proves nonnegativity, with equality only at \(s=t=0\).  Equation (6) then requires \(q=0\).  Thus (4) is an equality exactly when \(s=t=q=0\).  Substitution at this equality set gives
\[
g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B)=\frac{521}{1200}.
\tag{7}
\]

For the minimax loss, let \(\lambda=1407/2635\in(0,1)\) and \(v=2613/8432\).  Since a maximum dominates every convex combination,
\[
\begin{aligned}
w(B)-v
&\ge \lambda\ell_B(c_L)+(1-\lambda)\ell_B(c_U)-v\\
&=\frac{3N_{\mathrm{mm}}}{210800d},
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
where exact reduction gives
\[
N_{\mathrm{mm}}
=274734\left(q-\frac{70411}{137367}st\right)^2
+s^2\left(34527-\frac{439017980}{137367}t^2\right).
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(t^2\le9\), the second coefficient is bounded below by
\[
34527-9\frac{439017980}{137367}
=\frac{87967621}{15263}>0.
\tag{10}
\]
Hence equality in (9) requires \(s=q=0\).  Since \(\lambda\in(0,1)\), equality in the first line of (8) additionally requires \(\ell_B(c_L)=\ell_B(c_U)\).  Under \(s=q=0\), exact substitution gives
\[
\ell_B(c_L)-\ell_B(c_U)
=-\frac{3(55t^2-216)}{10(4t^2+243)},
\tag{11}
\]
so equality holds exactly when \(t^2=216/55\).  This proves the displayed minimizer equality set and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=2613/8432\).

Both equality sets are nonempty.  For the nominal set choose an orthogonal pair of norm \(\sqrt3\) in \(\mathbf1^\perp\).  For the minimax set choose a norm-\(\sqrt3\) vector \(y\) with \((\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55<9\), and then choose a norm-\(\sqrt3\) vector \(x\) perpendicular to both \(\mathbf1\) and \(y\).  On either equality set, (2) is diagonal and
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus the equality sets lie in \(\mathcal B_{1/8}\), proving \(\kappa\)-feasibility and membership of \(\xi_0\) in \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\).  Finally,
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\frac4{27}-\frac18=\frac5{216},
\tag{13}
\]
which are the claimed full-correspondence gap and regularity slack.  Assumption ass:known-exposure supplies the causal interpretation of the two exposure labels.  \(\square\)

\[

\begin{cases}

\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]

\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]

\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},

\[

\]

\[

\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}

defs.def:argmax-correspondences:
On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), define the primary full-quotient equality correspondences
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0),
\]
which may be empty.  On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction retain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\), and \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as regular deployable correspondences.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:dominance-gap: \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).  Since every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), the second term equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\).
defs.def:lawful-instance-class: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.
defs.def:separation-search-handle: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and analyze simultaneously the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance-surrogate correspondences.  The instance-specific certificate consists of exact optimizer equality sets, a rational lower bound \(\delta>0\) on \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and a rational optimizer-wide regularity slack \(\eta>0\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).  This finite lawful separation handle is distinct from, and does not assert, generic finite-\(\varepsilon\) termination of the moment-complete projective interval branch-and-bound procedure.
defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).
defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:certified-output: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:product-coupling-zero: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).
assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:kappa-feasibility: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

For a normalized representative \(B(x,y)\), put
\[

\qquad t=\mathbf1^{\top}y,
\qquad q=x^{\top}y.
\]
Direct block multiplication using (1) yields
\[
S_B=
\begin{bmatrix}
4/9-16s^2/729&-4q/27+68st/729\\
-4q/27+68st/729&2/3+8t^2/729
\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
With
\[
d=729+12t^2-36s^2-54q^2+68qst-22s^2t^2,
\tag{3}
\]
one has \(\det S_B=8d/19683\), so \(d>0\) on \(\mathcal B_{1/8}\).  Exact substitution in def:gain-loss gives
\[
\frac{31}{80}-g_B(0)=\frac{N_0}{1200d},
\tag{4}
\]
where
\[
N_0=5022q^2-4352qst+670s^2t^2+1629s^2+2148t^2.
\tag{5}
\]
The following completion makes its sign and equality set explicit:
\[
N_0
=5022\left(q-\frac{1088}{2511}st\right)^2
+1629s^2+2148t^2-\frac{685118}{2511}s^2t^2.
\tag{6}
\]
The last three terms are bilinear in \((s^2,t^2)\in[0,9]^2\).  Their values at the four vertices are
\[

\]
respectively.  Bilinear interpolation therefore proves nonnegativity, with equality only at \(s=t=0\).  Equation (6) then requires \(q=0\).  Thus (4) is an equality exactly when \(s=t=q=0\).  Substitution at this equality set gives

lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\xi_j=(\nu_j,F_{1j},F_{0j})\to\xi_0\).  Total-variation convergence on the finite assignment space gives
\[
\Pi_j\to\Pi_0,
\qquad
\Omega_j\to\Omega_0.
\tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity at \(\xi_0\) makes \(\Pi_j^{-1}\to\Pi_0^{-1}\) after discarding finitely many indices.  Wasserstein convergence on \([0,1]\) gives convergence of the first and second marginal moments.  Applying lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity to the continuous product map \((y_1,y_0)\mapsto y_1y_0\) gives
\[
c_{Lj}\to c_{L0},
\qquad
c_{Uj}\to c_{U0}.
\tag{2}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) and def:moment-matrix imply convergence of both endpoint matrices.

Work with the normalized representatives on the product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres, modulo the finite residual sign action.  This ambient quotient is compact.  The function
\[
\rho(\xi,B)=\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}
\tag{3}
\]
is jointly continuous, and \(\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)=\{B:\rho(\xi,B)\ge\kappa\}\).  On this closed region, \(S_B^{-1}\) has norm at most \((n\kappa)^{-1}\).  Hence (1)--(2), def:gain-loss, and the maximum over the two endpoints show that
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto g_{B,\xi}(0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(\xi,B)\longmapsto w_\xi(B)
\tag{4}
\]
are jointly continuous wherever \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\).

Put \(v_j=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)\).  Choose \(B_*\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\).  The assumed slack gives \(\rho(\xi_0,B_*)\ge\kappa+\eta\); by (3), \(B_*\) is feasible at \(\xi_j\) for all large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}v_j
\le\lim_{j\to\infty}w_{\xi_j}(B_*)
=v_0.
\tag{5}
\]

Next define
\[
q_j=\min_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B).
\]
Compactness makes the minimum well defined.  For a subsequence realizing \(\liminf_jq_j\), choose \(B_j\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)\) with \(w_{\xi_j}(B_j)=q_j\).  Compactness gives a further subsequence, not relabeled, with \(B_j\to\bar B\).  Closedness of the feasibility inequalities gives \(\bar B\in\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi_0)\).  Choose any \(C_*\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Its assumed slack makes it feasible at \(\xi_j\) eventually.  Since \(B_j\) maximizes the nominal gain,
\[
g_{B_j,\xi_j}(0)\ge g_{C_*,\xi_j}(0).
\]
Passing to the limit by (4) gives
\[
g_{\bar B,\xi_0}(0)\ge g_{C_*,\xi_0}(0)
=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi_0)}g_{B,\xi_0}(0),
\]
so \(\bar B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  A final use of (4) yields
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}q_j
=w_{\xi_0}(\bar B)
\ge q_0.
\tag{6}
\]
Since def:dominance-gap gives \(\Delta(\xi_j)=q_j-v_j\), (5)--(6) imply
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\ge\liminf_jq_j-\limsup_jv_j
\ge q_0-v_0
=\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
This is the claimed lower semicontinuity.  \(\square\)
