1,&\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0
\text{ and }\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,\\
2,&\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0.
\end{cases}
\]
The basis component is the encoded CAD pilot selector.  This construction is defined only on the exact rational or real-algebraic input domain and is distinct from the classical countable selector \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\); equality is not asserted.

For the stable rule, augment the exact input by exact rational or real-algebraic encodings of \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), \(\overline a\ge1\), and the population endpoint input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\); denote the augmented input by \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{st},+}\).  Impose, in addition to the normalized signed-pivot charts and coordinate inequalities \(|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), exactly one of
\[
\operatorname{tr}(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
\det(S_B)=0,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(S_B)\ge n\lambda_{1,n},
\]
or
\[
S_B-n\lambda_{2,n}I_2\succeq0.
\]
These are the rank-zero, rank-one, and rank-two pieces of \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).  Run the empirical rank-stratified CAD minimization over their union and, separately on the exact population endpoint input, isolate \(v_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The finite stable record \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD,st},+}\) contains an algebraic stable basis \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD,st},+}\), empirical stable-value bounds, exact rank and coordinate-envelope signs, the spectral-isolation record, and numbers \(\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}\) and \(\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}\) satisfying
\[
0\le\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
\le b_n^{\mathrm{st}}
\le\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
-\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
\le\varepsilon_m.
\]
The population endpoint augmentation is necessary only for the enclosure of the population stability price; empirical endpoint input alone cannot certify that price.  The exact-input stable CAD selector is distinct from both countable selectors, and no agreement, zero-tolerance selector, uniform complexity bound, or finite arbitrary-real algorithm is asserted.
defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
Let
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
A block class has rational support when each nonzero arm column is the squared-norm-\(n\) normalization of a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb Q^n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  In a fixed enumeration of the finitely many signed pivot charts, enumerate all rational-support block classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and call the resulting sequence \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), take \(C_k=[0]_+\) for every \(k\).

The following countable rule is a classical nonconstructive measurable existence construction, not a finite evaluation algorithm.  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]
The countable infimum and first qualifying index supply no finite stopping test for arbitrary real-valued pilot observations.  A separate rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic rule is defined only for exact rational or real-algebraic endpoint inputs; agreement between that rule and \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) is not asserted.

For the stable carrier \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\), fix once and for all a countable dense sequence \((C_k^{\mathrm{st}})_{k\ge1}\).  Compactness makes such a sequence exist and continuity of the rank-stratified objective gives
\[
\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}\widehat w_m^+(B)
=\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min\left\{k\ge1:
\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m\right\},
\qquad
\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+}
=C_{\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}}^{\mathrm{st}}.
\]
This stable selector is pilot measurable and obeys
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m.
\]
For arbitrary real pilot values it is, like the unrestricted countable rule, a nonconstructive measurable existence selector with no finite stopping test.  It is distinct from the unrestricted selector and from the exact-input stable cylindrical-algebraic selector.

On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The classical unrestricted countable selector has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\); it is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The stable selector instead trades unrestricted value against the certified positive-eigenvalue and coordinate constraints through \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).
defs.def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata:
Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
For the directed local neighborhoods in \(\texttt{ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate}\), retain \(\mathcal G_n=\{(\ell,j):j\in N_\ell\}\) only as a directed relation and define
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{k\ell}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\lvert N_\ell\rvert.
\]
No separated-set independence or undirected dependency-graph property is included in these definitions.

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

Fix displayed constants \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), and define the stable carrier
\[
\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{1,n}(\lambda_{1,n},\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{2,n}(\lambda_{2,n},\overline a).
\]
It is nonempty because the all-zero class belongs to \(\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)\), and it is compact in the normalized quotient.  Define the attained stable value and its exact approximation price relative to the unrestricted published carrier by
\[
v_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}w^+(B),
\qquad
b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=v_n^{\mathrm{st}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\ge0.
\]
Rank zero is exactly the uncontrolled Horvitz--Thompson fallback.  No equality \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=0\) and no rate for \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) is part of the definition.

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: For \(N=2n\) and every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the directed neighborhood satisfies \(\ell\in N_\ell\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the variable \(D_\ell\) is independent under \(\nu\) of the entire subvector \((D_j)_{j\notin N_\ell}\), and \(\lvert N_\ell\rvert\le\overline d n^\alpha\).

node.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds.  Let \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\) be the fixed enumeration of normalized rational-support classes of maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\) specified in \(\texttt{def:pilot-plugin}\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, this enumeration is nonempty and, for every realized pilot sample,
\[
 \inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k)
 =\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B).
\]
For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), the index
\[
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\left\{k\ge1:
 \widehat w_m^+(C_k)
 \le \inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j)+\varepsilon_m
 \right\}
\]
is finite and pilot-measurable.  Hence \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}\) is a measurable class of rank \(r_\Omega\) in the note's quotient of Zhao's published carrier and satisfies
\[
 \widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
 \le
 \inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]
The selector is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  This is a classical nonconstructive measurable existence selector: no full-carrier minimizer or zero-tolerance selector is used, no finite method for evaluating the countable infimum or certifying the first qualifying index on arbitrary real pilot inputs is supplied, and agreement with the exact-input cylindrical-algebraic selector is not asserted.
node.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix the design.  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let \(\widehat H_e\) be the comonotone or antimonotone quantile coupling of the two empirical marginals.  If
\[
\mathcal Y=(Y_1(1),\ldots,Y_n(1),-Y_1(0),\ldots,-Y_n(0))^{\top}
\]
under \(\widehat H_e^{\otimes n}\), the endpoint construction in \(\texttt{def:pilot-plugin}\) gives
\[
\widehat Q_e=\mathbb E_{\widehat H_e^{\otimes n}}(\mathcal Y\mathcal Y^{\top})\succeq0.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently
\[
\widehat A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}\widehat Q_e\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0.
\tag{2}
\]
For every carrier class, cyclicity of trace and \(\texttt{lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction}\) write the empirical endpoint residual as
\[
\widehat\ell_{B,e}^+
=\widehat h_e-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_B\widehat A_e),
\qquad e\in\{L,U\},
\tag{3}
\]
where \(\widehat h_e=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Q_e)\) is independent of \(B\).

We first show density in objective value on the maximal-rank stratum.  If \(r_\Omega=2\), positive definiteness of \(B^{\top}\Omega B\) is open, rational directions are dense in every signed-pivot chart, and normalization is continuous away from zero.  Hence normalized rational-support rank-two classes exist and are dense in each rank-two chart.  On a fixed rank stratum the projector, and thus (3), is continuous.

If \(r_\Omega=1\), let \([B]_+\) have rank one.  At least one arm column has nonzero image \(z_a=\Omega^{1/2}B_ae_a\).  Choose nonzero rational vectors converging to that arm direction.  Their images remain nonzero eventually.  Put the normalized rational vector in arm \(a\) and zero in the other arm.  The resulting class has rank one because maximal rank is one, and its one-dimensional projector converges to the projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega^{1/2}B)\).  These classes occur in \((C_k)\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), every projector is zero and the repeated zero class prescribed by \(\texttt{def:pilot-plugin}\) is nonempty and has every carrier value.

Now fix any \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\).  The approximation clause of \(\texttt{lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction}\) supplies maximal-rank classes \([B_j]_+\) and a projector \(P_\infty\) such that
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty,
\qquad P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) and trace monotonicity imply, endpoint by endpoint and then after taking the maximum,
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}\widehat w_m^+(B_j)\le\widehat w_m^+(B).
\tag{5}
\]
Approximate each fixed \(B_j\) by the rational-support classes just constructed.  It follows that, for every \(\delta>0\), some \(C_k\) satisfies
\[
\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\widehat w_m^+(B)+\delta.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking infima and letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) proves
\[
\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k)
=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B),
\tag{7}
\]
the reverse inequality being immediate because every \(C_k\) belongs to the carrier.  No cross-rank continuity or attainment is used.

For measurability, empirical means, variances, and endpoint cross moments are measurable functions of finitely many pilot order statistics.  Hence \(X_k:=\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\) is pilot measurable for each fixed \(k\), and \(\rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}X_j\) is measurable as a countable infimum.  Strict positivity and finiteness of \(\varepsilon_m\) make the qualifying set nonempty.  Moreover,
\[
\{\widehat k_m=k\}
=\{X_k\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\}
\cap\bigcap_{j<k}\{X_j>\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
\tag{8}
\]
so \(\widehat k_m\) is finite and measurable.  The selected class has rank \(r_\Omega\), obeys the asserted positive-tolerance inequality by (7), and has rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The argument supplies only a classical countable measurable selector; it supplies no finite arbitrary-real stopping rule, zero-tolerance selector, or agreement with the distinct exact-input CAD selector. \(\square\)

thm:encoded-cad-pilot-selector-certifica.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The algebraically encoded empirical input contains finitely many rational or real-algebraic entries of \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(\widehat Q_L\), and \(\widehat Q_U\), together with an exactly encoded \(\varepsilon_m>0\).  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined over the same real-algebraic coefficient field.  Each empirical endpoint matrix is positive semidefinite: as in (1) of the selector proof, it is the second-moment matrix under the appropriate empirical quantile coupling.  Thus the empirical input satisfies every algebraic support and positivity condition used by \(\texttt{thm:zhao-pseudoinverse-rank-stratified-epsilon-solver}\), with \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\) replaced by \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\).

Apply that theorem to the empirical endpoint pair.  Its rank-stratified graph uses, for \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq0\), the exact formulas
\[
S_B^+=0\quad\text{if }\operatorname{tr}(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
S_B^+=\frac{S_B}{\{\operatorname{tr}(S_B)\}^2}
\quad\text{if }\operatorname{tr}(S_B)>0,\ \det(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
S_B^+=\frac{\operatorname{adj}(S_B)}{\det(S_B)}
\quad\text{if }\det(S_B)>0.
\tag{1}
\]
All denominators in (1) are strictly positive on their stated strata.  After clearing them, the normalized signed-pivot charts, ranks, two endpoint residuals, and their maximum are a finite semialgebraic graph.  Real-closed-field quantifier elimination therefore isolates the empirical infimum
\[
\widehat v_m^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)
\]
and terminates with algebraic bounds satisfying
\[
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\widehat v_m^+
\le\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\qquad
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
-\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\le\varepsilon_m.
\tag{2}
\]
The defining property of the infimum and \(\varepsilon_m>0\) make the strict empirical \(\varepsilon_m\)-sublevel nonempty.  CAD lifting supplies a normalized rational or real-algebraic sample in it, giving
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})
\le\widehat v_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to verify the augmented rank and spectral record.  The selected matrix \(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}\) is a \(2\times2\) positive-semidefinite matrix with real-algebraic entries.  Its characteristic polynomial is
\[
\chi_m(t)=t^2-\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})t
+\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}).
\tag{4}
\]
Exact sign determination for the algebraic trace and determinant gives precisely rank zero, one, or two according as
\[
\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,
\quad
\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0=\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}),
\quad\text{or}\quad
\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Exact real-algebraic root isolation applied to (4) terminates and returns the distinct roots, multiplicities, exact zero tags, and disjoint rational isolating intervals for all positive roots.  Retaining the finite CAD projection and lifting records, the value isolations in (2), the sample in (3), and the spectral data (4)--(5) gives exactly \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\).  Each conclusion is checked by finite algebraic sign and interval arithmetic.  Nothing identifies this finite exact-input output with the arbitrary-real countable selector or supplies a complexity bound or zero-tolerance rule. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and let \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^+\) be an algebraically encoded empirical endpoint input from \(\texttt{def:encoded-cad-pilot-selector}\), with exactly encoded \(\varepsilon_m>0\).  Put
\[
\widehat v_m^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B).
\]
The fixed rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure terminates and returns \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\).  Its basis component has rational or real-algebraic coordinates, and
\[
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\widehat v_m^+
\le\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\qquad
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
-\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\varepsilon_m,
\]
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})
\le\widehat v_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\]
The selected-rank field is exact and belongs to \(\{0,1,2\}\), and \(\widehat{\mathscr S}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}}\) gives exact zero-versus-positive eigenvalue decisions and rational isolating intervals for all distinct positive eigenvalues, with multiplicities.  All conclusions are locally checkable from the finite CAD, algebraic-value, rank, and spectral records.  No agreement with the countable selector, zero-tolerance selector, complexity bound, or finite algorithm for arbitrary real-valued pilot inputs is asserted.

defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:encoded-cad-pilot-selector:
Call a realized pilot input algebraically encoded when \(\Pi,\Omega,\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\), all scalar endpoint fields needed to construct the empirical moment matrices, and a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\) have exact rational or real-algebraic encodings.  Denote it by \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^+\).  Fix once and for all the variable, projection, rank, signed-pivot-chart, cell, and algebraic-sample orders in the rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure.  Run that procedure with \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\) replaced by \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\), and write the augmented finite output as
\[
\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
=\left(
\widehat r_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}},
[\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}]_+,
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\widehat{\mathscr S}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}},
\widehat{\mathscr P}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\right).
\]
Here \(\widehat{\mathscr P}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\) is the finite CAD sign, sample, and value-isolation record, and the selected basis has normalized rational or real-algebraic coordinates.  Put
\[
\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}
=(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})^{\top}
\Omega\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}.
\]
The spectral record contains the characteristic polynomial
\[
\chi_m(t)=t^2-\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})t
+\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}),
\]
exact real-algebraic representations of its distinct roots with multiplicities, rational isolating intervals for every positive root, exact zero tags, and exact sign certificates for
\[
\widehat r_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}}=
\begin{cases}
0,&\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,\\
1,&\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0
\text{ and }\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,\\
2,&\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0.
\end{cases}
\]
The basis component is the encoded CAD pilot selector.  This construction is defined only on the exact rational or real-algebraic input domain and is distinct from the classical countable selector \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\); equality is not asserted.

For the stable rule, augment the exact input by exact rational or real-algebraic encodings of \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), \(\overline a\ge1\), and the population endpoint input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\); denote the augmented input by \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{st},+}\).  Impose, in addition to the normalized signed-pivot charts and coordinate inequalities \(|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), exactly one of
\[
\operatorname{tr}(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
\det(S_B)=0,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(S_B)\ge n\lambda_{1,n},
\]
or
\[
S_B-n\lambda_{2,n}I_2\succeq0.
\]
These are the rank-zero, rank-one, and rank-two pieces of \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).  Run the empirical rank-stratified CAD minimization over their union and, separately on the exact population endpoint input, isolate \(v_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The finite stable record \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD,st},+}\) contains an algebraic stable basis \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD,st},+}\), empirical stable-value bounds, exact rank and coordinate-envelope signs, the spectral-isolation record, and numbers \(\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}\) and \(\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}\) satisfying
\[
0\le\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
\le b_n^{\mathrm{st}}
\le\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
\overline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
-\underline b_{n,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st}}
\le\varepsilon_m.
\]
The population endpoint augmentation is necessary only for the enclosure of the population stability price; empirical endpoint input alone cannot certify that price.  The exact-input stable CAD selector is distinct from both countable selectors, and no agreement, zero-tolerance selector, uniform complexity bound, or finite arbitrary-real algorithm is asserted.
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
Let
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
A block class has rational support when each nonzero arm column is the squared-norm-\(n\) normalization of a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb Q^n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  In a fixed enumeration of the finitely many signed pivot charts, enumerate all rational-support block classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and call the resulting sequence \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), take \(C_k=[0]_+\) for every \(k\).

The following countable rule is a classical nonconstructive measurable existence construction, not a finite evaluation algorithm.  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]
The countable infimum and first qualifying index supply no finite stopping test for arbitrary real-valued pilot observations.  A separate rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic rule is defined only for exact rational or real-algebraic endpoint inputs; agreement between that rule and \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) is not asserted.

For the stable carrier \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\), fix once and for all a countable dense sequence \((C_k^{\mathrm{st}})_{k\ge1}\).  Compactness makes such a sequence exist and continuity of the rank-stratified objective gives
\[
\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}\widehat w_m^+(B)
=\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min\left\{k\ge1:
\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m\right\},
\qquad
\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+}
=C_{\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}}^{\mathrm{st}}.
\]
This stable selector is pilot measurable and obeys
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m.
\]
For arbitrary real pilot values it is, like the unrestricted countable rule, a nonconstructive measurable existence selector with no finite stopping test.  It is distinct from the unrestricted selector and from the exact-input stable cylindrical-algebraic selector.

On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The classical unrestricted countable selector has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\); it is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The stable selector instead trades unrestricted value against the certified positive-eigenvalue and coordinate constraints through \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).
defs.def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata:
Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
For the directed local neighborhoods in \(\texttt{ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate}\), retain \(\mathcal G_n=\{(\ell,j):j\in N_\ell\}\) only as a directed relation and define
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{k\ell}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\lvert N_\ell\rvert.
\]
No separated-set independence or undirected dependency-graph property is included in these definitions.

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

Fix displayed constants \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), and define the stable carrier
\[
\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{1,n}(\lambda_{1,n},\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{2,n}(\lambda_{2,n},\overline a).
\]
It is nonempty because the all-zero class belongs to \(\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)\), and it is compact in the normalized quotient.  Define the attained stable value and its exact approximation price relative to the unrestricted published carrier by
\[
v_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}w^+(B),
\qquad
b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=v_n^{\mathrm{st}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\ge0.
\]
Rank zero is exactly the uncontrolled Horvitz--Thompson fallback.  No equality \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=0\) and no rate for \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) is part of the definition.

assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: For \(N=2n\) and every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the directed neighborhood satisfies \(\ell\in N_\ell\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the variable \(D_\ell\) is independent under \(\nu\) of the entire subvector \((D_j)_{j\notin N_\ell}\), and \(\lvert N_\ell\rvert\le\overline d n^\alpha\).

node.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and let \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^+\) be an algebraically encoded empirical endpoint input from \(\texttt{def:encoded-cad-pilot-selector}\), with exactly encoded \(\varepsilon_m>0\).  Put
\[
\widehat v_m^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B).
\]
The fixed rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure terminates and returns \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\).  Its basis component has rational or real-algebraic coordinates, and
\[
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\widehat v_m^+
\le\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\qquad
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
-\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\varepsilon_m,
\]
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})
\le\widehat v_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\]
The selected-rank field is exact and belongs to \(\{0,1,2\}\), and \(\widehat{\mathscr S}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}}\) gives exact zero-versus-positive eigenvalue decisions and rational isolating intervals for all distinct positive eigenvalues, with multiplicities.  All conclusions are locally checkable from the finite CAD, algebraic-value, rank, and spectral records.  No agreement with the countable selector, zero-tolerance selector, complexity bound, or finite algorithm for arbitrary real-valued pilot inputs is asserted.
node.justification: This is the finite, checkable algorithmic counterpart to the deliberately nonconstructive countable selector.
node.gap: It applies only to exact rational or real-algebraic empirical endpoint inputs and makes no arbitrary-real or complexity claim.
node.consumer: Exact-input pilot deployments can audit rank, value tolerance, and spectral stability before using the observable estimator.
node.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The algebraically encoded empirical input contains finitely many rational or real-algebraic entries of \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(\widehat Q_L\), and \(\widehat Q_U\), together with an exactly encoded \(\varepsilon_m>0\).  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined over the same real-algebraic coefficient field.  Each empirical endpoint matrix is positive semidefinite: as in (1) of the selector proof, it is the second-moment matrix under the appropriate empirical quantile coupling.  Thus the empirical input satisfies every algebraic support and positivity condition used by \(\texttt{thm:zhao-pseudoinverse-rank-stratified-epsilon-solver}\), with \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\) replaced by \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\).

Apply that theorem to the empirical endpoint pair.  Its rank-stratified graph uses, for \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq0\), the exact formulas
\[
S_B^+=0\quad\text{if }\operatorname{tr}(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
S_B^+=\frac{S_B}{\{\operatorname{tr}(S_B)\}^2}
\quad\text{if }\operatorname{tr}(S_B)>0,\ \det(S_B)=0,
\]
\[
S_B^+=\frac{\operatorname{adj}(S_B)}{\det(S_B)}
\quad\text{if }\det(S_B)>0.
\tag{1}
\]
All denominators in (1) are strictly positive on their stated strata.  After clearing them, the normalized signed-pivot charts, ranks, two endpoint residuals, and their maximum are a finite semialgebraic graph.  Real-closed-field quantifier elimination therefore isolates the empirical infimum
\[
\widehat v_m^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)
\]
and terminates with algebraic bounds satisfying
\[
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\le\widehat v_m^+
\le\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\qquad
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
-\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\le\varepsilon_m.
\tag{2}
\]
The defining property of the infimum and \(\varepsilon_m>0\) make the strict empirical \(\varepsilon_m\)-sublevel nonempty.  CAD lifting supplies a normalized rational or real-algebraic sample in it, giving
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})
\le\widehat v_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to verify the augmented rank and spectral record.  The selected matrix \(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}\) is a \(2\times2\) positive-semidefinite matrix with real-algebraic entries.  Its characteristic polynomial is
\[
\chi_m(t)=t^2-\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})t
+\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}).
\tag{4}
\]
Exact sign determination for the algebraic trace and determinant gives precisely rank zero, one, or two according as
\[
\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,
\quad
\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0=\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}),
\quad\text{or}\quad
\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Exact real-algebraic root isolation applied to (4) terminates and returns the distinct roots, multiplicities, exact zero tags, and disjoint rational isolating intervals for all positive roots.  Retaining the finite CAD projection and lifting records, the value isolations in (2), the sample in (3), and the spectral data (4)--(5) gives exactly \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\).  Each conclusion is checked by finite algebraic sign and interval arithmetic.  Nothing identifies this finite exact-input output with the arbitrary-real countable selector or supplies a complexity bound or zero-tolerance rule. \(\square\)

lem:full-carrier-plugin-objective-regret.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), \(\texttt{lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction}\) supplies the orthogonal projector
\[
P_B=\Omega^{1/2}B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega^{1/2},
\]
so \(0\preceq P_B\preceq I_{2n}\).  Congruence by \(\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\), licensed by exposure positivity, gives
\[
0\preceq A_B^+
=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}
\preceq \Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}=A_{\mathrm{HT}}.
\tag{1}
\]
Both matrices are positive semidefinite, so their nuclear norms equal their traces.  Since \(D_{i,a}\) is Bernoulli of mean \(\pi_{i,a}\),
\[
\Omega_{(i,a),(i,a)}=\pi_{i,a}(1-\pi_{i,a}).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus, with \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\),
\[
\lVert A_B^+\rVert_*
\le\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\sum_{i,a}\frac{1-\pi_{i,a}}{\pi_{i,a}}
\le2n\pi_{\min,n}^{-1},
\qquad
\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*le2n\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), the empirical and population loss definitions give
\[
\widehat\ell_{B,e}^+-\ell_B^+(c_e)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B^+)
\{\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\}\right].
\tag{4}
\]
Trace duality, (3), and the one-Lipschitz property of the maximum in the supremum norm imply
\[
d_m^+\le4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m.
\tag{5}
\]
Under \(\texttt{ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate}\), \(\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}\le\underline\pi^{-1}n^\beta\), which proves (A).

For the expectation rate, put \(D_a=W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)\).  On \([0,1]\), the distribution-function and quantile formulas for \(W_1\), Jensen's inequality, and the binomial variance identity give
\[
\mathbb E_PD_a
\le\int_0^1\sqrt{\frac{F_a(y)\{1-F_a(y)\}}{m_a}}\,dy
\le\frac1{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The one- and two-Lipschitz moment maps and
\(|xy-x'y'|\le|x-x'|+|y-y'|\) give
\[
|\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a|\le D_a,
\quad |\widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2|\le4D_a,
\quad |\widehat c_e-c_e|\le2(D_1+D_0).
\tag{7}
\]
Using the block formula for \(Q\), \(\lVert I_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), and \(\lVert\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=n\), there is a numerical \(K_M<\infty\) such that, for \(m=m_1\wedge m_0\),
\[
\mathbb E_PM_m\le K_M\frac n{\sqrt m}.
\tag{8}
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-countable-measurable-selector}\), pointwise in the pilot,
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\tag{9}
\]
For two functions on the same nonempty domain,
\[
|\inf f-\inf g|\le\sup|f-g|.
\tag{10}
\]
The carrier is nonempty because it contains the zero class.  Applying (10), (9), and the definition of \(d_m^+\) yields
\[
0\le w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\le2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{11}
\]
Taking expectations and using (A) proves (B).  Finally, (8) gives
\[
n\mathbb E_P\!\left[w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right]
\le8K_M\underline\pi^{-1}\frac{n^{1+\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+n\mathbb E_P\varepsilon_m\longrightarrow0.
\tag{12}
\]
The rank claim follows from the selector construction.  The proof controls the all-rank basis objective and does not assert an observable-estimator bridge at an uncontrolled singular rank. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
Under ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:unpaired-pilot, and ass:exposure-positivity, define
\[
 M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
 \qquad
 d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}
 |\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|,
\]
and let \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  For every rank zero, one, or two class \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\),
\[
 0\preceq A_B^+\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}},
 \qquad
 A_B^+=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1},
 \qquad
 A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 d_m^+\le 4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m.
\]
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, this yields
\[
 d_m^+\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}M_m
\tag{A}
\]
and, for every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]
 \le
 8\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}\mathbb E_P[M_m]
 +\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m].
\tag{B}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad n\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m]\longrightarrow0
\]
imply
\[
 n\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]\longrightarrow0.
\]
The selected class has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\).  This is a full-carrier basis-objective regret result on the note's quotient of Zhao's all-rank pseudoinverse domain, not a feasible-estimator variance bridge when the selected rank is singular.

defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
Let
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
A block class has rational support when each nonzero arm column is the squared-norm-\(n\) normalization of a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb Q^n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  In a fixed enumeration of the finitely many signed pivot charts, enumerate all rational-support block classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and call the resulting sequence \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), take \(C_k=[0]_+\) for every \(k\).

The following countable rule is a classical nonconstructive measurable existence construction, not a finite evaluation algorithm.  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]
The countable infimum and first qualifying index supply no finite stopping test for arbitrary real-valued pilot observations.  A separate rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic rule is defined only for exact rational or real-algebraic endpoint inputs; agreement between that rule and \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) is not asserted.

For the stable carrier \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\), fix once and for all a countable dense sequence \((C_k^{\mathrm{st}})_{k\ge1}\).  Compactness makes such a sequence exist and continuity of the rank-stratified objective gives
\[
\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}\widehat w_m^+(B)
=\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min\left\{k\ge1:
\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m\right\},
\qquad
\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+}
=C_{\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}}^{\mathrm{st}}.
\]
This stable selector is pilot measurable and obeys
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m.
\]
For arbitrary real pilot values it is, like the unrestricted countable rule, a nonconstructive measurable existence selector with no finite stopping test.  It is distinct from the unrestricted selector and from the exact-input stable cylindrical-algebraic selector.

On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The classical unrestricted countable selector has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\); it is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The stable selector instead trades unrestricted value against the certified positive-eigenvalue and coordinate constraints through \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata:
Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
For the directed local neighborhoods in \(\texttt{ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate}\), retain \(\mathcal G_n=\{(\ell,j):j\in N_\ell\}\) only as a directed relation and define
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{k\ell}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\lvert N_\ell\rvert.
\]
No separated-set independence or undirected dependency-graph property is included in these definitions.

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

Fix displayed constants \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), and define the stable carrier
\[
\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{1,n}(\lambda_{1,n},\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{2,n}(\lambda_{2,n},\overline a).
\]
It is nonempty because the all-zero class belongs to \(\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)\), and it is compact in the normalized quotient.  Define the attained stable value and its exact approximation price relative to the unrestricted published carrier by
\[
v_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}w^+(B),
\qquad
b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=v_n^{\mathrm{st}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\ge0.
\]
Rank zero is exactly the uncontrolled Horvitz--Thompson fallback.  No equality \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=0\) and no rate for \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) is part of the definition.

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate: There are constants \(\underline\pi>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that \(\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: For \(N=2n\) and every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the directed neighborhood satisfies \(\ell\in N_\ell\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the variable \(D_\ell\) is independent under \(\nu\) of the entire subvector \((D_j)_{j\notin N_\ell}\), and \(\lvert N_\ell\rvert\le\overline d n^\alpha\).

node.statement:
Under ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:unpaired-pilot, and ass:exposure-positivity, define
\[
 M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
 \qquad
 d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}
 |\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|,
\]
and let \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  For every rank zero, one, or two class \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\),
\[
 0\preceq A_B^+\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}},
 \qquad
 A_B^+=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1},
 \qquad
 A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 d_m^+\le 4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m.
\]
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, this yields
\[
 d_m^+\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}M_m
\tag{A}
\]
and, for every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]
 \le
 8\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}\mathbb E_P[M_m]
 +\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m].
\tag{B}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad n\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m]\longrightarrow0
\]
imply
\[
 n\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]\longrightarrow0.
\]
The selected class has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\).  This is a full-carrier basis-objective regret result on the note's quotient of Zhao's all-rank pseudoinverse domain, not a feasible-estimator variance bridge when the selected rank is singular.
node.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), \(\texttt{lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction}\) supplies the orthogonal projector
\[
P_B=\Omega^{1/2}B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega^{1/2},
\]
so \(0\preceq P_B\preceq I_{2n}\).  Congruence by \(\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\), licensed by exposure positivity, gives
\[
0\preceq A_B^+
=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}
\preceq \Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}=A_{\mathrm{HT}}.
\tag{1}
\]
Both matrices are positive semidefinite, so their nuclear norms equal their traces.  Since \(D_{i,a}\) is Bernoulli of mean \(\pi_{i,a}\),
\[
\Omega_{(i,a),(i,a)}=\pi_{i,a}(1-\pi_{i,a}).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus, with \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\),
\[
\lVert A_B^+\rVert_*
\le\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\sum_{i,a}\frac{1-\pi_{i,a}}{\pi_{i,a}}
\le2n\pi_{\min,n}^{-1},
\qquad
\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*le2n\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), the empirical and population loss definitions give
\[
\widehat\ell_{B,e}^+-\ell_B^+(c_e)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B^+)
\{\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\}\right].
\tag{4}
\]
Trace duality, (3), and the one-Lipschitz property of the maximum in the supremum norm imply
\[
d_m^+\le4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m.
\tag{5}
\]
Under \(\texttt{ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate}\), \(\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}\le\underline\pi^{-1}n^\beta\), which proves (A).

For the expectation rate, put \(D_a=W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)\).  On \([0,1]\), the distribution-function and quantile formulas for \(W_1\), Jensen's inequality, and the binomial variance identity give
\[
\mathbb E_PD_a
\le\int_0^1\sqrt{\frac{F_a(y)\{1-F_a(y)\}}{m_a}}\,dy
\le\frac1{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The one- and two-Lipschitz moment maps and
\(|xy-x'y'|\le|x-x'|+|y-y'|\) give
\[
|\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a|\le D_a,
\quad |\widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2|\le4D_a,
\quad |\widehat c_e-c_e|\le2(D_1+D_0).
\tag{7}
\]
Using the block formula for \(Q\), \(\lVert I_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), and \(\lVert\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=n\), there is a numerical \(K_M<\infty\) such that, for \(m=m_1\wedge m_0\),
\[
\mathbb E_PM_m\le K_M\frac n{\sqrt m}.
\tag{8}
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-countable-measurable-selector}\), pointwise in the pilot,
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\tag{9}
\]
For two functions on the same nonempty domain,
\[
|\inf f-\inf g|\le\sup|f-g|.
\tag{10}
\]
The carrier is nonempty because it contains the zero class.  Applying (10), (9), and the definition of \(d_m^+\) yields
\[
0\le w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\le2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{11}
\]
Taking expectations and using (A) proves (B).  Finally, (8) gives
\[
n\mathbb E_P\!\left[w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right]
\le8K_M\underline\pi^{-1}\frac{n^{1+\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+n\mathbb E_P\varepsilon_m\longrightarrow0.
\tag{12}
\]
The rank claim follows from the selector construction.  The proof controls the all-rank basis objective and does not assert an observable-estimator bridge at an uncontrolled singular rank. \(\square\)

lem:bounded-unpaired-endpoint-strong-con.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For arm \(a\), write \(F_{a,m_a}\) for the distribution function of \(\widehat F_a\).  For every rational \(t\in[0,1]\), the variables
\[
X_{j,a}(t)=\mathbf 1\{Y^P_{j,a}\le t\}
\]
are independent Bernoulli variables with mean \(F_a(t)\) by \(\texttt{ass:unpaired-pilot}\).  Hoeffding's elementary exponential argument gives, for \(s>0\),
\[
P\!\left(\left|F_{a,m_a}(t)-F_a(t)\right|>s\right)
\le 2e^{-2m_as^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, for a Bernoulli variable \(X\) of mean \(p\), convexity gives
\(\mathbb E e^{\lambda(X-p)}\le e^{\lambda^2/8}\); exponential Markov inequality, independence, and optimization in \(\lambda\) yield (1).  The right side is summable in \(m_a\).  Intersecting the resulting probability-one events over rational \(t\) and rational \(s>0\) shows that \(F_{a,m_a}(t)\to F_a(t)\) simultaneously at every rational \(t\).

Fix \(K\ge1\) and put \(x_j=j/K\).  Monotonicity of the two distribution functions implies, for \(y\in[x_j,x_{j+1}]\),
\[
|F_{a,m_a}(y)-F_a(y)|
\le \max_{r\in\{j,j+1\}}|F_{a,m_a}(x_r)-F_a(x_r)|
+F_a(x_{j+1})-F_a(x_j).
\tag{2}
\]
Integrating, summing, passing to the limit on the finite grid, and telescoping the last increments gives
\[
\limsup_{m_a\to\infty}\int_0^1|F_{a,m_a}(y)-F_a(y)|\,dy\le K^{-1}
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{3}
\]
Letting \(K\to\infty\) proves convergence of this integral to zero.  For probability laws \(R,S\) on \([0,1]\), the layer-cake representation and Tonelli's theorem give
\[
\int_0^1|R^{-1}(u)-S^{-1}(u)|\,du
=\int_0^1|R(y)-S(y)|\,dy.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus
\[
\int_0^1|\widehat F_a^{-1}(u)-F_a^{-1}(u)|\,du\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad a\in\{1,0\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The bounded support used in (2)--(5) is exactly \(\texttt{ass:bounded-outcomes}\).

The functions \(y\) and \(y^2\) are respectively one- and two-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\), so (5) yields convergence of the empirical means, second moments, and variances.  Moreover,
\[
|xy-x'y'|\le |x-x'|+|y-y'|
\qquad(x,x',y,y'\in[0,1]).
\tag{6}
\]
Applying (6) to the comonotone and antimonotone quantile pairs proves convergence of both empirical endpoint cross moments and hence of both empirical covariance endpoints.  Every block of \(\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) is therefore a convergent scalar multiplying either \(I_n\) or \(\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\).  Since \(n\) is fixed and
\[
\lVert I_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1,
\qquad \lVert\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=n,
\tag{7}
\]
we obtain
\[
M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely under }P.
\]
The additional stable and unrestricted selectors now present in \(\texttt{def:pilot-plugin}\) do not enter this endpoint calculation. \(\square\)

defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
Let
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
A block class has rational support when each nonzero arm column is the squared-norm-\(n\) normalization of a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb Q^n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  In a fixed enumeration of the finitely many signed pivot charts, enumerate all rational-support block classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and call the resulting sequence \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), take \(C_k=[0]_+\) for every \(k\).

The following countable rule is a classical nonconstructive measurable existence construction, not a finite evaluation algorithm.  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]
The countable infimum and first qualifying index supply no finite stopping test for arbitrary real-valued pilot observations.  A separate rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic rule is defined only for exact rational or real-algebraic endpoint inputs; agreement between that rule and \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) is not asserted.

For the stable carrier \(\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}\), fix once and for all a countable dense sequence \((C_k^{\mathrm{st}})_{k\ge1}\).  Compactness makes such a sequence exist and continuity of the rank-stratified objective gives
\[
\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}\widehat w_m^+(B)
=\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}}).
\]
For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min\left\{k\ge1:
\widehat w_m^+(C_k^{\mathrm{st}})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m\right\},
\qquad
\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+}
=C_{\widehat k_m^{\mathrm{st}}}^{\mathrm{st}}.
\]
This stable selector is pilot measurable and obeys
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{st},+})
\le\widehat v_m^{\mathrm{st}}+\varepsilon_m.
\]
For arbitrary real pilot values it is, like the unrestricted countable rule, a nonconstructive measurable existence selector with no finite stopping test.  It is distinct from the unrestricted selector and from the exact-input stable cylindrical-algebraic selector.

On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The classical unrestricted countable selector has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\); it is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The stable selector instead trades unrestricted value against the certified positive-eigenvalue and coordinate constraints through \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\).
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata:
Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
For the directed local neighborhoods in \(\texttt{ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate}\), retain \(\mathcal G_n=\{(\ell,j):j\in N_\ell\}\) only as a directed relation and define
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{k\ell}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\lvert N_\ell\rvert.
\]
No separated-set independence or undirected dependency-graph property is included in these definitions.

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

Fix displayed constants \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), and define the stable carrier
\[
\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{1,n}(\lambda_{1,n},\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{2,n}(\lambda_{2,n},\overline a).
\]
It is nonempty because the all-zero class belongs to \(\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)\), and it is compact in the normalized quotient.  Define the attained stable value and its exact approximation price relative to the unrestricted published carrier by
\[
v_n^{\mathrm{st}}
=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}w^+(B),
\qquad
b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=v_n^{\mathrm{st}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\ge0.
\]
Rank zero is exactly the uncontrolled Horvitz--Thompson fallback.  No equality \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}=0\) and no rate for \(b_n^{\mathrm{st}}\) is part of the definition.

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: For \(N=2n\) and every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the directed neighborhood satisfies \(\ell\in N_\ell\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the variable \(D_\ell\) is independent under \(\nu\) of the entire subvector \((D_j)_{j\notin N_\ell}\), and \(\lvert N_\ell\rvert\le\overline d n^\alpha\).

thm:zhao-pseudoinverse-plugin-value-and-.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put
\[
M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:bounded-unpaired-endpoint-strong-convergence}\),
\[
M_m\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely as }m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty.
\tag{1}
\]
Because the design and \(n\) are fixed and exposure positivity holds,
\(\pi_{\min,n}:=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  The uniform all-rank modulus in \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-plugin-objective-regret-rate}\) therefore gives
\[
d_m^+\le4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
The carrier is nonempty because it contains the zero class, and the elementary inequality
\[
|\inf f-\inf g|\le\sup|f-g|
\tag{3}
\]
applied on \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) yields
\[
\left|\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right|
\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{4}
\]

For every finite positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-countable-measurable-selector}\) gives a finite measurable index, a selected class of rank \(r_\Omega\), and
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\tag{5}
\]
Twice applying the uniform error gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
&\le\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)+d_m^+\\
&\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m+d_m^+\\
&\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Since \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is the infimum on the same carrier,
\[
0\le w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\le2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (2) and (7) prove the asserted regret convergence when \(\varepsilon_m\to0\) almost surely.  The selected rank is \(r_\Omega\), hence is two exactly when rank two is achievable.  The argument uses neither a zero-tolerance selector nor cross-rank argmin convergence, and the countable rule remains distinct from the exact-input CAD selector. \(\square\)
